transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because people keep acting like I’m making something up, like I don’t know my own house. But I know my wife’s relative came in there to get at me. My tools don’t just move by themselves, you know? I’ve worked with tools my whole life, I know where I put them.

And it’s not just that—every weekend I try to go fishing, something gets spoiled somehow. After months of it, you start seeing the pattern plain as day. He’s trying to take over my place, push me out, and everybody wants to say it’s nothing. That’s why I’m here.
Do you believe that people are trying to harm you or target you in some way?

Yes, I do. I mean, that’s why I’m here, because everybody keeps looking at me like I’m imagining it. But I know what’s happening in my own house. My wife’s relative came in there to get at me—my tools don’t just move themselves.

And it’s always when I’m trying to get a little peace, like fishing on the weekend. Something gets spoiled every time, and after months of that you start to see it. He’s trying to take over my place, push me out. People can call it whatever they want, but I know what I’m seeing.
Have you ever seen, heard, or felt things that others don't seem to notice, like voices, shadows, or strange sensations?

I don’t know about all that—voices and shadows, no, not like in the movies or anything. I’m not walking around seeing things that aren’t there.

What I notice is what’s in front of me, you know? Like when something’s been moved, or when a plan gets ruined right when I’m finally trying to relax. People act like that’s the same as “hearing voices,” but it’s not. I’ve been working with my hands since I got out of school, I know when something’s off.
Do you ever feel like someone is watching you or keeping track of your actions when you're not at home?

When I’m not home? I mean… I don’t know if he’s following me around town, if that’s what you mean. But I know he’s keeping track somehow, because every time I plan to do something—like go fishing on the weekend—it gets spoiled. That doesn’t just happen by accident over and over.

And the house, that’s the main thing. My tools, my things… I know where I put them. I worked as an assembler for years, you get a system, you know? People think a wrench just “turns up” somewhere else, but it doesn’t. My wife’s relative came in there to get at me, and everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it. He’s been trying to take over my place, push me out, and after months of it, it’s plain as day to me.
Do you ever feel like things in the environment, like TV broadcasts or random events, are specifically directed at you or meant to send you a message?

TV? No, I’m not saying the TV is talking to me or sending me codes or anything like that. That’s not what this is.

What I’m talking about is right in my own life, in my house. My wife’s relative coming in, my tools being moved—tools don’t just walk off. And then every time I try to get out and fish, just have a quiet weekend, something happens to spoil it. After months of that, you start putting it together. People keep acting like I’m imagining it, but I can see he’s trying to take over my place and push me out.
Do you ever have thoughts or beliefs that people have told you are not true, but you still believe them anyway, even if no one else seems to agree with you?

Yeah—well, that’s kind of why I’m here, isn’t it? Everybody keeps telling me I’m “imagining things” or “making too much of it,” but I know what’s been going on.

My wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. I know where I keep my tools—I’ve had a system my whole working life, you don’t just misplace things like that over and over. And it’s not just the tools, it’s like every time I make a plan to go fishing, finally get a little peace, something happens to ruin it. Once or twice, fine, maybe that’s life. But every weekend? For months?

People can say they don’t agree, but I can see it plain as day. He’s trying to take over my place and push me out.
Do you ever have any thoughts or ideas about what’s happening that you can’t explain to others in a way that makes sense, even though they seem completely obvious to you?

I can explain it fine, it’s just nobody wants to hear it straight. I mean, I worked with tools my whole life, you know, assembly work—if something’s put in one place, it stays there unless somebody moves it. That’s just common sense.

And I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know my wife’s relative came into the house to get at me. The tools don’t move themselves. And then the fishing—every weekend I try to make plans, just to get out and clear my head, and something happens to spoil it. Once, sure, maybe. But month after month? No.

So maybe I don’t say it the way they want me to, or they pretend it doesn’t make sense, but to me it’s plain as day. He’s trying to take over my place and push me out.
Are there any other things you believe are happening that others might find hard to believe or that you struggle to explain clearly, even though you feel certain they’re true?

Other things? I mean… it’s all kind of the same thing, isn’t it? People want me to list it out like I’m making a case in court, but I know what I’ve seen.

I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. My tools don’t move themselves. I had a system with my tools back when I was working assembly, you learn to keep things where they belong or the whole job goes sideways. And the fishing—every time I try to get out, just get a weekend to myself, something happens. Not once, not twice, every weekend for months.

So, no, I don’t have some wild story beyond that. It’s right there in front of everybody. He’s been trying to take over my place and push me out, and I don’t know why everyone acts like that’s so hard to understand.
Do you ever feel that you can control things happening around you, like if your thoughts could influence what happens in your house or with your tools?

Control things? No, I don’t think it’s like that. I mean, if I could control things around the house, believe me, my tools would stay right where I put them.

I’ve never thought my thoughts were moving anything or making things happen. That sounds… I don’t know, that’s not what I’m saying. I’m talking about what actually happens in the house, like when you’ve got a place for a wrench or a bit and then it’s not there. Back on the line, if somebody left parts scattered, the whole job would get backed up, and then management would come down on everyone even if it wasn’t your fault.

So no, not my thoughts controlling things. I don’t know how else to say it.
Can you explain exactly how you know that your wife’s relative is the one moving your tools and spoiling your plans—have you seen them do it, or is it more of a feeling or conclusion you’ve reached?

I haven’t, you know, stood there with a flashlight and caught him with a screwdriver in his hand, if that’s what you mean. But that doesn’t mean I don’t know. People act like unless you have a picture of it, it didn’t happen.

I know because my tools don’t just move. I had them set up a certain way for years—when you work assembly, you learn that. Everything has a place. Then suddenly things are shifted, missing, put where I’d never put them. And every time I try to go fishing, something comes up, something gets spoiled. Once or twice, fine, maybe life happens. But every weekend, for months? Come on.

So no, it’s not just some “feeling.” It’s the pattern. It’s plain as day to me. He came into my house to get at me, and he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.
